successCriteria.description: `AuthSession` is exported from `web/src/modules/auth/auth-session.ts` with the exact canonical shape `{ token: string; profile: EmployeeProfile; status: AuthSessionStatus }`, importing `EmployeeProfile` and `AuthSessionStatus` from `web/src/shared/types/index.ts` (not re-declaring them).

`AuthService.login(email, password)` calls the injected `IApiClient.login`, persists the returned token via `ITokenStorage.setToken`, and resolves an `AuthSession` with `status: AuthSessionStatus.AUTHENTICATED`; a Vitest test asserts the token is stored and the returned session equals `{ token, profile, status: 'AUTHENTICATED' }`.

On login failure, `AuthService.login` propagates the server's error message verbatim (no email-existence hint added) and does not clear an already-stored token; a Vitest test asserts the rejection message equals the server's message and the pre-existing token survives.

`AuthService.logout()` clears the token via `ITokenStorage.clear()` and is idempotent (safe to call when already logged out); a Vitest test asserts the token is null after logout and a second call does not throw.

`AuthProvider` holds the current session in plain React state (no state-management library), exposes `login`/`logout`/`session`, and on mount re-initializes an authenticated session from a stored token (re-fetching the profile via `getMe`); `useAuth()` throws when used outside `AuthProvider`.
`web/src/modules/auth/index.ts` re-exports `IAuthService`, `AuthService`, `AuthProvider`, `useAuth`, and `AuthSession` (the barrel is the module's public entry point).

constraints: The anonymous/not-authenticated state is represented by a `null` session (not a session with `status: AuthSessionStatus.ANONYMOUS`); `logout` and the context provider both converge on this single representation.
Login failure must not reveal whether the email exists: surface the server's `ApiError.message` verbatim and add no email-existence hint; the API is enumeration-safe.

The auth module must not decode the JWT `exp` client-side or otherwise proactively detect expiry — token invalidation relies solely on the server's 401 (handled by the API client), per the binding rule.
No state-management library is introduced; the session lives in React state only.
The auth module performs no direct HTTP or storage access of its own — it depends on the injected `IApiClient` and `ITokenStorage` from `web/src/infrastructure/api/index.ts`.
outOfScope: No role-gated screens, manager/HR surfaces, or leave create/submit/approve/reject/cancel — the frontend is read-only for leave requests.
No proactive JWT expiry detection (client-side `exp` decoding) — token invalidation relies solely on the server's 401.
No UI component library or state-management library is introduced in this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: AuthSession has exactly the canonical shape `{ token: string; profile: EmployeeProfile; status: AuthSessionStatus }`; it is created on successful login with `status: AUTHENTICATED` and cleared (represented as `null`) on logout or any 401. It never carries `passwordHash` or `terminationDate` (those are absent from `EmployeeProfile`).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: On failure, propagate the server's error message verbatim without revealing whether the email exists; do not clear an already-stored token on a failed login.
Clears the token and returns to the anonymous (null-session) state; must not throw when already logged out.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: `AuthSession` must import `EmployeeProfile` and `AuthSessionStatus` from the shared-types module rather than re-declaring them, so the canonical field shapes and enum member sets stay single-sourced.

`AuthService` must depend on the injected `IApiClient` and `ITokenStorage` from the infrastructure API module (not a pool/client/db helper), matching the declared `auth -> api-client` dependency edge.

The `AuthSession` shape and the `auth` module's owned symbols (`IAuthService`, `AuthService`, `AuthProvider`, `useAuth`, `AuthSession`) must match the reconciled architecture's `auth` module boundary and the `AuthSession` domain entity.

integrationPoints.why: AuthService consumes the API client's login/getMe and the token storage's getToken/setToken/clear; the API client owns bearer-header and 401-clearing behaviour.
AuthSession and AuthService assemble the canonical session from the shared profile type and session-status enum.
